name: Columbia Gas Transmission Line MB Extension Project

values.StartLocation: Owings Mills Metering and Regulation Station

researcher_notes: The line is built and in service. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission environmental assessment notice of April 29, 2013 (docket CP13-8) describes 21.1 miles of 26-inch pipeline in Baltimore and Harford counties, Maryland, starting at the Owings Mills metering station, proposed by Columbia Gas Transmission LLC. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects table for August 2026 (sheet Historical Projects 1996-2024, Excel row 781) lists the project as completed on October 28, 2014, 21 miles, 26 inches, cost 132 million dollars, docket CP13-8. Those are two independent origins. No existing row covers it: the roster has only the whole-system row P0169 and other named Columbia expansion rows. At 21.1 miles (about 34 km) it passes the 25 km length rule. End location (Fallston area, from the consolidator note) was not confirmed in a verified source, so it is left blank. The trade magazine page on the approval did not load the 21.1 figure through the checker and is not cited. Pipeline Parent was not researched. Route not researched; it parallels the company's Line MA, so an official map or filing should be used for a route later. Note the EIA cost is a project cost stated in millions and staged in full dollars.
